title: Formal bi-entire weighted-coefficient completion and radius-loss derivative bridge
question: Does the formal bi-entire coefficient topology admit a representation-independent weighted-l1 completion with dense finite polynomials, submultiplicative Cauchy product, and explicit radius-loss derivative bounds?

model.completion: finite-support coefficient arrays are dense in weighted l1; the weighted l1 array space is complete
model.interpretation: formal coefficient Banach/Frechet intermediate; no physical Q3 representation is identified

scoped_verdict: The weighted coefficient array space is a complete normed algebra; finite-support arrays converge by weighted tail truncation; Cauchy product is submultiplicative; formal field/source derivatives are continuous after explicit radius loss. The construction is representation-independent only at the coefficient-algebra level.

adversarial_review.check: Completeness is for weighted coefficient arrays, not an unbounded CCR operator closure or a physical observable algebra.
The finite-support truncation theorem uses absolute weighted summability; finite fixtures do not replace that theorem.
Derivative bounds require strictly smaller radii and do not give a same-radius generator bound.
A Banach coefficient product does not establish Q3 Duhamel word incidence, cancellation, or spatial first-passage decay.
R224 checks rational fixture identities only; it does not formalize the infinite weighted-l1 theorem.
No KMS, OS reflection positivity, GNS gap, continuum limit, C6, Sector A or Pre-A closure follows.

scope.not_closed: The physical Q3 common-core representation, energy/state bridge, repeated histories, spatial first-passage, exhaustion, common alpha, KMS/OS reconstruction, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.

next_action: Use the formal completion only as a candidate target for an explicit Q3 common-core map; then prove or refute continuity of the actual shifted-force/history map into it with volume and orientation control.
no_overclaim: This package proves a formal weighted coefficient completion and radius-loss calculus. It does not prove an operator-domain completion, Q3 dynamics, a thermodynamic QFT, common alpha, KMS, a GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, Pre-A, TECT production or a Clay result.
